transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because of my eating at night. Once I start, it’s like I’m watching myself do it and telling myself to stop, but I just keep reaching for more anyway. It feels like I’m not really in control of it.
Do you find yourself having episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, even when you’re not hungry?

Yes. Some evenings I’ll start with just leftovers, and then it turns into sandwiches, cereal, cookies, whatever snacks are in the pantry. It’s way more than I’d ever normally put on a plate for supper, and I’m not really eating because I’m hungry at that point.
Does this eating behavior cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life?

Yes, it does. I’m still getting to work and handling my basic responsibilities, but it’s affecting my life. I’ve been turning down plans, like going to the theater or walking with my club, because I feel ashamed and I get stuck thinking about whether I look disciplined enough. It’s… it’s embarrassing, and it takes up a lot of my mind.
Do these episodes usually happen after you've already gone to bed and woken up during the night, or are you still up and about when they start?

I’m not completely sure. I haven’t really paid close attention to that difference. I just know it tends to happen at night, but whether it’s after I’ve gone to bed and woken up or while I’m still up… I’d have to think about it more.
Do you feel like you're not in control during these episodes, even if you're not physically hungry? Like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Yes. That’s honestly what brings me in. Once I start eating at night, it feels like I’m watching myself do it and telling myself, “Stop, that’s enough,” but my hands just keep going back for more. I don’t feel in control of it.
Do these episodes usually happen after you’ve woken up in the middle of the night, or are they more likely to start while you’re still up and about in the evening?

I’m honestly not sure. I know it’s usually at night, but I haven’t really sorted out whether I had already gone to sleep and woke up, or if I was just still awake in the evening. I’d probably need to pay closer attention to that.
Do you usually start eating during these episodes after you've already gone to bed and woken up in the middle of the night?

I don’t know for sure. I haven’t really kept track of whether I’d already gone to bed and then woke up, or if I was just still awake when it started. It’s just kind of all “nighttime” in my mind right now.
Do you usually start eating during these episodes after you've already gone to bed and then wake up in the middle of the night?
I still can’t say for sure. I know it happens at night, but I haven’t paid close enough attention to whether I was already asleep and woke up, or if I just hadn’t gone to bed yet.

Can you tell me if, during these episodes, you feel like you’re eating a much larger amount of food than most people would in a similar period of time, and if it feels like you can’t stop yourself even if you want to?

Yes. Once I start eating at night, it feels like I’m watching myself do it and telling myself, “Stop, that’s enough,” but I don’t stop. My hands just keep going back for more, even when I don’t want to keep eating.
Can you tell me if you start eating even when you’re not physically hungry, and if so, does it feel like you’re eating a much larger amount than most people would in a short time?

Yes. A lot of times I’m not really hungry when I start. I might just begin with some leftovers, and then it turns into sandwiches, cereal, cookies, whatever snacks are around. It’s way more than I’d ever normally sit down and eat for supper.
Do you often find yourself eating large amounts of food at night even when you’re not physically hungry?

Yes. Some nights I’m not really hungry, but I’ll start with leftovers and then just keep going—sandwiches, cereal, cookies, whatever’s in the pantry. It ends up being way more than I’d ever put on a plate for a normal supper.
Can you tell me if you usually start eating during these episodes after you’ve already gone to bed and then wake up in the middle of the night?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close enough attention to whether I’ve already been asleep and then wake up. I just know it tends to happen at night, but I can’t say for sure it’s after I’ve gone to bed.
Do you usually start eating these large amounts of food only after you’ve woken up during the night, or does it often begin while you’re still awake and not yet in bed?
I can’t really say for sure. I know it happens at night, but I haven’t tracked whether I was already asleep and woke up, or if I was still up and just hadn’t gone to bed yet.
Can you tell me if these nighttime eating episodes usually happen after you’ve already fallen asleep and then wake up in the middle of the night?
I’m sorry, I really don’t know. I haven’t noticed it clearly enough to say whether I’d already fallen asleep and woke up, or if it was just late and I was still awake.
Can you tell me if these nighttime eating episodes usually happen after you’ve already fallen asleep and then wake up in the middle of the night?
I still can’t really tell. I haven’t been paying attention to whether I was actually asleep first and then woke up. I just know it’s at night, but I don’t know the exact pattern.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed that these nighttime eating episodes usually start after you’ve already fallen asleep and then wake up in the middle of the night?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t really noticed whether I’d already been asleep and then woke up, or if it was just late and I hadn’t gone to bed yet.
Can you tell me if you often start eating these large amounts of food only after you’ve woken up in the middle of the night, or does it often begin while you’re still awake and not yet asleep?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t kept track of whether it starts after I’ve been asleep and wake up, or if I’m just still up late when it happens. I just know it’s nighttime.
Can you tell me if you often start eating these large amounts of food only after you’ve woken up in the middle of the night, or does it often begin while you’re still awake and not yet in bed?

I’m sorry, I really don’t know. I haven’t been paying close enough attention to whether I’d been asleep and woke up, or if I was just still awake and ended up eating. It’s just kind of blurred together as “nighttime” for me.
Can you tell me if your nighttime eating has caused you to avoid social situations or withdraw from activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, it has some. I’m still getting to work and handling the basic things I need to do, but I’ve been turning down plans more lately. Like theater outings or walks with my walking club. I just feel ashamed, and I get caught up worrying whether I look like I have enough discipline, if that makes sense.
Can you tell me if you often start eating these large amounts of food only after you’ve woken up in the middle of the night, or does it often begin while you’re still awake and not yet asleep?

I still don’t really know. I haven’t been able to separate it out like that—whether I had already fallen asleep and woke up, or whether I was just up too late and it started then. I just remember it as happening at night.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the core diagnostic criteria for Night Eating Syndrome (F50.71), including recurrent episodes of night eating, lack of control over eating behavior during these episodes, and significant psychosocial distress. The episodes occur at night, and while the patient cannot specify whether they occur after sleep onset or while still awake, the pattern is consistent with night eating rather than strictly nocturnal. There is no evidence supporting anorexia nervosa (F50.0) or bulimia nervosa (F50.01), which require additional features like fear of weight gain, body shape concerns, or compensatory behaviors.
